head_commit.message:
Give the deploy gate permission to read the answer it refuses without

With `05 Security` finally green on main, `03 Deploy` still failed in 14 seconds at the same
step it has always failed at. The step's own output says why, and it is not the scan:

    SECURITY GATE: 05 Security must have passed for 6c5660a1
      GitHub API returned 403; refusing rather than guessing.

`03-deploy.yml` declared NO `permissions:` block, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` got the repository default
-- contents and packages, not `actions`. `scripts/require_security_scan.py` asks
`GET /repos/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=...` whether the scan passed for the commit being
deployed, and that endpoint requires the `actions` scope. Without it the API answers 403, the
gate treats an unreadable answer as a failed gate, and nothing deploys.

The gate is RIGHT to do that. "I could not find out" is not evidence of safety, and the
script says so in its own docstring. It was refusing correctly on information it was not
allowed to fetch.

TWO FAULTS, ONE SYMPTOM, AND THAT IS WORTH RECORDING. Every `03 Deploy` run has failed in
11-14s at this step. The bandit finding fixed in f1376280 was real and did independently fail
`05 Security`, so the gate was correctly refusing a genuinely-failed scan. This 403 was
sitting behind it the whole time and could not be seen until the first cause was cleared and
the scan went green. Fixing the visible cause of a fail-closed gate does not mean the gate
will open; it means the next reason becomes visible.

Set explicitly rather than widened: `contents: read` for `actions/checkout`, `actions: read`
for that one query. Nothing in this workflow needs more -- AWS auth uses static access keys
rather than OIDC, so no `id-token: write`, and `actions/upload-artifact@v4` needs no token
scope of its own. Both are named because declaring the block REPLACES the default for every
job in the workflow, so omitting `contents` would break the checkout.

Verified: the YAML parses, both jobs (`pre-deployment-validation`, `ecs-deployment`) and the
workflow `env` are unchanged, and the gate step is still second in the job. Whether the gate
now passes is answered by the next run, which this push triggers.

head_commit.message:
D5': align the real-Redis gate database and add production-path quota coverage

Three paths, no production code.

1. .github/workflows/01-pr-check.yml  (+2/-2)
   AERORA_TEST_REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/15 -> /0, in BOTH places that set it
   (the `unit-tests` job and the `d5-redis-diagnostics` job). The application cache is
   pinned to REDIS_DB_CACHE = 0 by backend_app/backend/redis_manager.get_redis_url(), which
   overrides whatever database a URL names, so a gate pointed at /15 PINGed a database the
   application never writes to. The diagnostics job itself is otherwise untouched and the
   provisioning-and-isolation job is not modified.

2. tests/test_webhook_duplicate_delivery_real_redis.py  (383 -> 646 lines)
   The test client now derives its URL from the application's own
   get_redis_url(REDIS_DB_CACHE) instead of reading AERORA_TEST_REDIS_URL, and a
   bidirectional sentinel probe proves the test client and the cache manager observe the
   same keyspace before any assertion runs. A mock or absent cache now FAILS rather than
   skipping. All six existing tests are preserved; there are no executable skips.

   This addresses the two failures in run 38047483583
   (test_the_lock_is_recorded_in_redis_under_the_documented_key and
   test_an_in_flight_delivery_blocks_a_concurrent_one), which were measuring an empty
   database rather than a dedup defect.

3. tests/test_quota01_metered_reservation_is_hard.py  (264 -> 530 lines)
   Adds the first real-Redis coverage of the PRODUCTION quota path; the pre-existing
   real-Redis test re-implemented reserve_quota's algorithm in the test body and so proved
   only that Redis INCR/DECR are atomic.
     * test_production_reserve_quota_admits_exactly_the_limit_against_real_redis
     * test_production_zero_allowance_writes_no_meter_against_real_redis
   All seven existing tests are preserved.

NOT included, deliberately:
  * tests/test_quota01_exchange_slot_is_atomic.py is retained unchanged. Its 21 failures are
    caused by the slot-guard implementation being absent from this branch, not by this
    change. Removal was not authorized.
  * No change to backend_app/core/subscription_dependencies.py or
    backend_app/routers/exchange.py. store_keys still wraps its vault write without the
    guard, so the QUOTA-01 read-then-write race remains live and exchange-slot concurrency
    and release safety remain UNPROVEN, pending a separately authorized workstream.

head_commit.message:
Let the CI Redis service reach the tests that exist to use it

`tests/conftest.py` blanks REDIS_URL at import so the 11,000-test lane cannot be
re-pointed at a live cache. That is correct and is left alone. Its consequence was
that the healthy `redis:7-alpine` service in the `unit-tests` job could never switch
on the three real-Redis test files: they read REDIS_URL, found '', and skipped on
every PR.

AERORA_TEST_REDIS_URL is the second, deliberate name -- the same pattern
AERORA_TEST_DATABASE_URL already uses for PostgreSQL -- and conftest does not touch
it, so it survives to the shared gate in tests/real_redis_gate.py.

The gate keeps three outcomes apart: opt-in unset SKIPS, configured-but-unreachable
FAILS (a dead Redis in CI must not look like a green run), reachable RUNS. Verified
locally for the first two; the third is what this change exists to exercise.

Scope note: this does NOT close QUOTA-01. The metered concurrency test drives a raw
Redis client and mirrors reserve_quota's increment-first-revert inline; it does not
call SubscriptionEngine.reserve_quota, so the production reservation path remains
unverified against a real server. Recorded in
staging/PHASE11B_A7_D5_CI_VERIFICATION.md.

No application code, no production path, and no other workstream's changes are
included. Live trading remains OFF / NOT CERTIFIED.

workflow_runs.name: 01 PR Check
workflow_runs.display_title: D5': point the real-Redis tests at the CI redis service

head_commit.message:
D5': point the real-Redis tests at the CI redis service

The three real-Redis test files could never run in CI. They gated on
`AERORA_TEST_REDIS_URL or REDIS_URL` and tested only the shape of the string, and
`tests/conftest.py` blanks `REDIS_URL` unconditionally at import so the 11,000+ test
lane cannot be re-pointed at a live cache. The `redis:7-alpine` service in the
`unit-tests` job was therefore healthy, mapped and health-checked, and exported under a
name the gate could never read: the tests skipped on every PR, one of them since the day
it was written.

The workflow now also exports `AERORA_TEST_REDIS_URL` (database index 15), the second
deliberate name -- the same pattern `AERORA_TEST_DATABASE_URL` already uses for
PostgreSQL. `REDIS_URL` is retained unchanged, because other tests assert on how the
application behaves when it is present.

`tests/real_redis_gate.py` now owns the decision for every real-Redis test, and keeps
three states apart that were previously two:

    opt-in unset            SKIP   the only legitimate skip
    opt-in set, no server   FAIL   you asked for a real Redis; there isn't one
    opt-in set, reachable   RUN

A non-loopback host is refused unless `AERORA_TEST_REDIS_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`, and no URL,
host or credential appears in any message the gate produces.

The webhook file additionally stopped converting a cache-manager fallback into a skip.
Once the gate has confirmed the endpoint answers PING, a `MockRedisClient` or `None` from
`_get_active_cache()` is a wiring fault rather than an absent server, and it now fails --
a skip there would have shown six tests green against a broken service while the three
quota tests failed on the same one.

No application code changes. The reachable-Redis path has never executed anywhere, which
is what this PR exists to establish.
